items.summary: Teams of AI agents barely outperform solo agents but cost up to 5.1x more, according to Vals AI. Only one out of four tests with GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 showed a measurable gain.

items.title: What is Decision 3.0? vLLM Semantic Router’s New Open Decision Models
items.summary: vLLM Semantic Router released Decision 3.0, 5 Apache-2.0 multimodal decision models from 0.8B to 27B. They answer choice, yes/no and score questions about text and images in one call, without generating text.

items.title: Meet Cloudflare Clef-omni: A 30B-A3B Multimodal Decision Model for Audio, Video, Image and Text
items.summary: Cloudflare released Clef-omni, an Apache-2.0 multimodal decision model built on Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B. It scores text, images, audio and video in one call for $0.15 per million input tokens, while Clef-flash drops to $0.038.

items.title: TII Releases Falcon-ASR: 1.6B Arabic Speech Model Hits 20.92% WER
items.summary: TII has released Falcon-ASR, a 1.6B speech recognition model for Arabic with an Emirati focus. It reports 20.92% average WER on 6 Arabic test sets, but weights and an API are not yet available.

items.title: Top 12 AI Live Translation Tools in 2026: Latency, Languages, Pricing
items.summary: We checked 12 AI live translation tools, including Palabra.ai, Google Live Translate, DeepL Voice, Teams Interpreter and Wordly, against official pages for languages, latency, platforms and pricing. The post Top 12 AI Live Translation Tools in 2026: Latency, Languages, Pricing appeared first on MarkTechPost .

items.title: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Nexus solved dozens of open math problems and actually got peer reviewed
items.summary: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Nexus solved dozens of open math problems, including nine Erdős problems two of which were unsolved for 56 years, per a study in Science. The publication comes as OpenAI faces a boycott for dumping AI proofs on GitHub without peer review.

items.summary: This White Paper provides roboticists and control engineers with a comprehensive overview of how motion planning and motion tracking can be decoupled to preserve professional athletic style in humanoid robots, and why adaptive, speed-aware control is essential for closing the gap between simulation and real-world deployment. items.title: We Specified an AI Agent in 2016. We Called It Analytics.
items.summary: Re-reading my own IBM patent on real-time concert feedback as what it actually was: an agentic loop with multimodal perception, memory-grounded inference, and a human in the loop. What it got right, and what a decade of hindsight teaches agent builders today.

items.summary: The second-largest corporate employer has bet big on robot workers to scale.

items.title: Anthropic's Andrej Karpathy says "the external world has seen the preview" of what AI can actually do
items.summary: Andrej Karpathy, co-founder of OpenAI and now at Anthropic, sees a widening knowledge gap in AI. About 75 percent of the world's population has barely touched LLMs.

items.title: Microsoft’s new AI chip makes it less reliant on Nvidia’s GPUs
items.summary: Microsoft is announcing its third-generation Maia in-house AI chip today, designed to be the "primary AI inference system" for Microsoft's products and services. Maia 300 not only improves the cost and efficiency of running AI workloads in the cloud, it's also more capable of handling the latest reasoning models and agentic tasks.

items.title: White House reverses course and restores UK AI Safety Institute's access to frontier models
items.summary: The White House has reversed course and restored the UK's AI Security Institute's early access to AI models from Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and OpenAI. In September, the Trump administration had told the companies to stop sharing their models with the British agency.

items.title: Microsoft plans to scale its own Maia AI chips to gigawatt levels by 2027
items.summary: Microsoft will make its in-house Azure Maia chips the main AI inference system across its products starting in 2027, deploying them at multi-gigawatt scale. The upcoming Maia 300 should deliver 40 percent more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems.

items.title: Simulating student learning for better AI tutoring
items.summary: StudentSim is a research system for evaluating and improving AI tutoring tools before they are tested with learners. It models how individuals may engage with tutors, giving feedback to improve tutor performance across subjects like chess, writing, and mathematics.

items.title: Turning Opportunistic AI Inference Capacity Into Better Ads Recommendations
items.summary: At Meta, we’ve built a system that enhances ads recommendations by leveraging idle inference capacity in our fleet. Two elasticity levers in the system allow ads recommendation work to expand across opportunistic capacity, without compromising baseline performance.

items.title: Shipping Media Over QUIC at Meta Scale for Instagram Live Ingest
items.summary: Meta has begun deploying Media over QUIC (MoQ), an emerging open protocol for real-time video streaming at scale. MoQ will help simplify our protocol stack for live streaming video and enhance overall user experience for live video.

items.title: Clearing chat history helps AI agents find better solutions
items.summary: Microsoft researchers found that autonomous AI agents get trapped in what they call "idea basins" because of their growing chat context, local solution regions they can't escape. Their "Fork-and-Flush" method clears the chat history but keeps the workspace, achieving up to 66 percent better results on the same compute budget.

items.title: Meta has some Wonder Full new AI models
items.summary: Meta is making up for lost time in the AI race. After launching Muse Spark, the first model from its revamped Superintelligence Labs division, and buzzy AI agent Muse, it's now launching two new models it claims can go toe-to-toe with the industry's best.

items.title: Muse Wonder Puts Meta Back at the AI Frontier
items.summary: Meta’s biggest model rivals the world’s best—and includes new features to keep agents from going off the rails.

items.title: Sakana AI's self-improving model gets better at solving and judging, but can't catch its own blind spots
items.summary: Sakana AI's MASS method lets one language model improve itself by solving tasks, judging results, and refining workflows, reaching a win rate of nearly 70 percent against the base model after two rounds. But when the model misses the same errors across all three roles, it can mistake them for progress and reinforce them during training.

items.title: Meet the Anthropic Engineer Keeping Its AI Agent Trustworthy
items.summary: If you’ve ever wondered how Claude and similar AI agents can answer complex questions in seconds and where they get the information, you’re not alone. Gurmeet Saran works to find that answer every day as an engineer at Anthropic in San Francisco, the AI research company behind Claude.

items.summary: At AI Engineer New York, Anthropic drew on lessons from Unix and Linux to explain how agents can tackle bigger projects without overwhelming developers.

items.summary: Meta's new Muse Wonder models rank in the top three on six out of ten benchmarks, with the biggest gains in agentic tasks. But the cost per task has nearly tripled.

items.title: OCP Summit 2026: Powering AI with Open Innovations in Scale-Up, Scale-Out, and Scale-Across Networks

Flattened Planar Fabric (FPF), a multiplane backend scale-out fabric that fundamentally changes how GPUs connect to the network MetaRoCE, our open-source AI transport protocol.

items.title: Alibaba Qwen Introduces QwenGyre: Elastic Reinforcement Learning RL for XLong-Horizon Agents
items.summary: Alibaba’s Qwen team has introduced QwenGyre, an elastic reinforcement learning RL framework for extreme-long-horizon agent training. QwenGyre is an online reinforcement learning system from Alibaba that trains coding agents through unmodified, black-box harnesses.

items.title: From Earth to Orbit, France’s Ecosystem Delivers Agentic Computing at Scale With NVIDIA
items.summary: Companies in France are deploying agentic computing across industries spanning space, financial services, the public sector and scientific research, demonstrating how the country’s ecosystem has moved from ambition to application. France’s progress sits on deliberate groundwork.

items.title: Z.ai GLM-Legal Beats Claude Fable 5 and Kimi K3 on Harvey LAB
items.summary: Z.ai’s GLM-Legal is a legal AI model built on GLM-5.3-Flash. It scores 19.2% all-pass on Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark, nearly 3x its base, at $0.15 per test.

items.title: AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models
items.summary: When Keelan Miskell began winding down his crypto startup this year, he didn’t think its data was worth much: the users were anonymous, the company just a few years old. But he’s since turned the firm’s digital archives into real money.

items.title: Anthropic study warns that small AI models could soon replicate across everyday devices
items.summary: Small AI models may be just months away from spreading on their own across poorly secured consumer devices like smart TVs and robot vacuums, according to a new Anthropic study. In tests, one model already completed the full infection chain.
